sentences.text: Early researchers visualized this animal as an excessively elongated reptile based on the arrangement of its tail bones.
The head was described as conical with eyes positioned on top and a pelican-like jaw to help swallow prey.
One early belief held that the creature possessed only front flippers and lacked rear flippers entirely.
Its distinctive elongated and cylindrical premaxilla may have been used to ram prey or during fights with other individuals.
The earliest known fossils likely date back before the 1500s and were probably found by Native American peoples.
In 1804, the Lewis and Clark Expedition found a fossil skeleton near the Missouri River that was identified as a 45-foot-long fish.
The type specimen was found in the late 1860s by Colonel John Butler Conyngham and Mr. Minor in the Niobrara Formation near Fort Hays, Kansas.
Edward Drinker Cope presented a preliminary description of this specimen in 1869 after borrowing it from Louis Agassiz.
The largest species, T. rex, is estimated to have reached over 13 meters in length and weighed nearly 8.4 tons.
T. proriger was among the largest mosasaurs, with the largest specimens reaching lengths of 12.8 to 13.7 meters.
Fossil evidence indicates Tylosaurus engaged in intraspecific combat and acted as an apex predator consuming fish, birds, sea turtles, plesiosaurs, and other mosasaurs.
Tylosaurus possessed an endothermic metabolism, a trait unlike that of nearly all modern squamates.
The genus Tylosaurus was established by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1872.
The type species of the genus Tylosaurus is Macrosaurus proriger.
Known species include T. proriger, T. nepaeolicus, T. ivoensis, T. iembeensis, T. kansasensis, and T. rex.
Tylosaurus fossils date to the Late Cretaceous.
T. proriger lived from the late Santonian to mid-Campanian in North America, including Kansas, Alabama, and Nebraska.
Fossils of Tylosaurus have been found primarily around the North Atlantic Ocean, including in North America, Europe, and Africa.
The locality of the Tylosaurus rex holotype indicates it originated from the Wolfe City Formation, though its exact stratigraphic position is uncertain.
Some authors argue that the genus Hainosaurus should remain distinct from Tylosaurus based on dental traits, despite the 2016 transfer of H. bernardi to Tylosaurus.
A 2008 discovery of Taniwhasaurus in Japan revived the hypothesis that T. ivoensis might belong to that genus, though authors consider this a topic for future study.
Caldwell and Jiménez-Huidobro questioned the distinction between Tylosaurus kansasensis and T. nepaeolicus in 2013.
A 2016 study led by Caldwell interpreted Tylosaurus kansasensis as a juvenile form of T. nepaeolicus, treating it as a junior synonym.
